items.shape:

A self-contained .ipynb for Google Colab: first cell clones the repo (git clone + pip install -e .), a setup cell detects and configures the Colab runtime's accelerator (jax.devices() after selecting GPU/TPU runtime in Colab's own Runtime menu -- Colab's JAX auto-detects the assigned accelerator; no manual JAX_PLATFORMS override should be needed once the notebook runtime type is set to GPU or TPU), then runs scripts/cortical_column_localized_workflow.py's build_config()/construct()/simulate() pipeline and reports real wall-clock timing on whatever hardware Colab actually assigns (which varies run to run -- T4/L4/A100 for GPU, v2-8/v5e for TPU, not user-selectable to a specific SKU on free/Colab-Pro tiers).

GPU/TPU speed estimate (reasoned prior for the notebook's own before-you-run section, NOT a measured claim -- must be labeled as an estimate, confirmed only once the notebook actually runs on real hardware): the dominant per-step cost is jax.ops.segment_sum over ~10M edges (scatter-add pattern), not dense matmul. GPUs (A100) are historically well-suited to scatter/gather-heavy sparse workloads via flexible memory addressing; TPUs are optimized primarily for dense matmul/convolution and are typically LESS efficient on scatter-add patterns than GPUs of comparable class -- so a naive 'TPU is always faster' assumption likely does NOT hold for this specific workload; expect a CUDA A100 to outperform a TPU here, not the reverse. Rough order-of-magnitude prior for a A100 vs this session's CPU baseline (527s for 10,000 steps): commonly-seen JAX CPU->GPU speedups for segment_sum/scan-heavy sparse workloads of this size are roughly 10-50x, which would put an A100 run at very roughly 10-50s for the same 1000ms/10,000-step simulate() -- but this is a genuine estimate range, not a benchmark; construct()'s own cost (currently a host-side/non-traced numpy loop, NOT GPU-accelerated at all per this session's own design choice) would NOT speed up on GPU/TPU and would remain ~231s regardless of accelerator -- worth flagging prominently in the notebook so a user doesn't expect construct() itself to benefit from the Colab GPU/TPU runtime.

items.title: Migrate 3 scripts' un-consolidated build_model/apply_drive_correction copies onto hdp_network.py's generic versions
items.shape:
All return Model from incomparable inputs (HDPColumnConfig vs dict vs no-arg) -- the y3=f1(x1,x2) merge pattern. jaxfne/hdp_network.py's own module docstring already claims to have consolidated 'the near-duplicate build_model/apply_drive_correction pairs previously copy-pasted across scripts/hdp_1000_laminar_column_boosted.py and scripts/hdp_100_stability_sweep.py' -- but a repo-wide AST scan (2026-06-30) found 3 MORE scripts with their own un-migrated copies that the original consolidation missed. Fix: each script's build_model/apply_drive_correction should construct an HDPColumnConfig from its local parameters and delegate to hdp_network.build_model/apply_drive_correction, deleting the local duplicate body.

RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-07-01 (Progress pass): the "mechanical merge, delete local duplicate body" shape above is WRONG for 2 of 3 target scripts -- verified with real construct() calls, not assumed:
1. scripts/hdp_suite2_visualizations.py: ALREADY correctly consolidated (its build_model/apply_drive_correction are thin wrappers delegating to hdp_network.build_model(base.CFG)/apply_drive_correction(model, base.CFG), base.CFG is a real HDPColumnConfig from hdp_1000_laminar_column_boosted.py). The original AST scan finding was stale for this file -- no action needed, this part of the item is DONE.
2. scripts/hdp_1000_neuronal_tensor_column.py: apply_drive_correction is NOT semantically equivalent to hdp_network.apply_drive_correction. hdp_network's version is a MULTIPLICATIVE correction on the model's EXISTING drive (corrected = existing_drive * factor). This script's version is an ABSOLUTE OVERRIDE (drive = BASE_DRIVE_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT[ct] * DRIVE_CORRECTION_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT[ct], ignoring the tensor-built model's existing drive entirely). Confirmed empirically: the tensor-first construct() path gives pre-correction drive E=5.0/PV=3.0/SST=3.5/VIP=3.0 (NeuronType.make defaults), not 4.0-for-all -- a blind delegate to the multiplicative helper would silently compute a DIFFERENT final drive than the absolute-override this script currently produces. This is a real would-be bug, not a style nitpick.
3. scripts/spectrolaminar_tfne_izhikevich_pipeline.py: build_model does NOT pass baseline_drive_by_cell_type to laminar_cortex_config (leaves it None -> "uses emitter preset defaults" per builders.py's own docstring). Confirmed empirically: laminar_cortex_config with baseline_drive_by_cell_type=None gives the SAME preset (E=5.0/PV=3.0/SST=3.5/VIP=3.0) as case 2 above -- NOT hdp_network.HDPColumnConfig's default BASE_DRIVE_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT (4.0-for-all). Delegating build_model to hdp_network.build_model would silently change every neuron's baseline drive from the emitter preset to 4.0-for-all.

ROOT CAUSE (shared by both remaining scripts): hdp_network.HDPColumnConfig.base_drive_by_cell_type has no "use emitter preset, do not override" sentinel -- it always supplies an explicit dict. laminar_cortex_config supports baseline_drive_by_cell_type=None for exactly this passthrough case; HDPColumnConfig cannot currently express it.

REVISED FIX (not done this pass -- a real design change, correctly out of scope for a quick consolidation): either (a) give HDPColumnConfig.base_drive_by_cell_type an Optional[...] = None default that build_model passes through as None to laminar_cortex_config unchanged, and give apply_drive_correction a mode flag (multiplicative vs absolute-override) -- OR (b) leave these 2 scripts un-merged since their baseline-drive behavior is intentionally different from the canonical HDP column default and forcing them onto it would change their science, not just their code shape.

CLOSED 2026-07-03: the remaining scripts/spectrolaminar_tfne_izhikevich_pipeline.py gap was reclassified as an intentional design boundary, not a migration gap -- see skills/FRICTIONS_STACK.md F-023's closure note. HDPColumnConfig is deliberately the simple/canonical-6-layer wrapper; this script needs a non-canonical 5-layer/flat-fraction shape that Configuration.area_layer_cell_types already supports directly. Extending HDPColumnConfig to cover every possible shape was considered and rejected as adding complexity to the wrong layer, contradicting the 0.4.7 'simple code, complex configs' design goal (see config-schema-ic-pcb-redesign).
items.note:
UPDATE 2026-07-02 (Progress pass, F-023 design fix): the REVISED FIX's option (a) landed. jaxfne/hdp_network.py::HDPColumnConfig.base_drive_by_cell_type is now Optional[Mapping[str,float]]=None (was a mandatory dict-default field) -- None means 'do not pass baseline_drive_by_cell_type to laminar_cortex_config at all', genuinely forwarding to the emitter preset (verified via real build_model() calls: None config gives E=5.0/PV=3.0/SST=3.5/VIP=3.0; explicit BASE_DRIVE_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT gives 4.0-flat). apply_drive_correction(model, cfg, mode=) got a mode='multiplicative'|'absolute' flag ('multiplicative' is the default, byte-identical to the pre-change function body; 'absolute' computes drive=cfg.base_drive_by_cell_type[ct]*cfg.drive_correction_by_cell_type[ct], ignoring the model's existing drive).

BLOCKING-CALLER CHECK (step 4d of the task): grepped all HDPColumnConfig(...) call sites repo-wide (scripts/hdp_100_stability_sweep.py, scripts/hdp_1000_laminar_column_boosted.py, scripts/hdp_v2_rho_sweep.py, scripts/hdp_fi_calibration_curves.py) -- none passed base_drive_by_cell_type explicitly, so the None-default change would have silently flipped all 4 from 4.0-flat to preset. Fixed all 4 by adding explicit base_drive_by_cell_type=dict(BASE_DRIVE_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT) at each call site (import added where missing). Verified via real build_model() calls that each of the 4 still produces 4.0-flat drive post-fix (E/PV/SST/VIP all =4.0). hdp_suite2_visualizations.py inherits the fix transitively (imports base.CFG from hdp_1000_laminar_column_boosted.py) -- re-verified its build_model(base.CFG) also still gives 4.0-flat.

SCRIPT MIGRATION (step 5) -- 2 of 3 target scripts:
1. scripts/hdp_suite2_visualizations.py: unaffected, still correctly consolidated (no change needed, confirmed still delegates to hdp_network.build_model/apply_drive_correction).
2. scripts/hdp_1000_neuronal_tensor_column.py: MIGRATED. Its local apply_drive_correction (absolute override) now delegates to hdp_network.apply_drive_correction(model, cfg, mode='absolute') with an inline HDPColumnConfig carrying its own BASE_DRIVE_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT/DRIVE_CORRECTION_BY_CELL_TYPE_DEFAULT. Verified BITWISE IDENTICAL to the old hand-rolled loop via a real build_tensor()+construct() run (max abs diff = 0.0 across all 4 cell types, E/PV/SST/VIP checked individually). NOTE: this script's Model still comes from the tensor-first jtfne.construct(tensor, RuntimeConfiguration(...)) path, NOT from hdp_network.build_model -- that part was never migrated (and correctly should not be: this script's circuit is a bespoke NeuronalTensor with explicit inter-laminar E-E motifs that HDPColumnConfig cannot express, a structurally different network from the canonical HDPColumnConfig laminar column, not a copy-paste duplicate). Only the drive-correction logic was a genuine duplicate; that part is now consolidated.
3. scripts/spectrolaminar_tfne_izhikevich_pipeline.py: NOT migrated, deliberately left open. Its build_model has no drive-correction call at all (grepped, confirmed) so mode-flag risk doesn't apply here -- but its network shape is structurally incompatible with HDPColumnConfig: 5 layers with a merged 'L2/3' label (vs HDPColumnConfig's canonical 6-layer L1..L6 split) and a single flat cell_type_fractions dict applied uniformly via area_layer_cell_types (vs HDPColumnConfig's per-layer LAYER_CELL_TYPE_FRAC_DEFAULT table). Forcing this onto HDPColumnConfig would require either extending HDPColumnConfig to support flat/uniform cell-type fractions and arbitrary layer sets (a second design change, out of scope for this pass) or building a bespoke HDPColumnConfig subclass/config that doesn't cleanly express this script's exact layer taxonomy -- neither is a safe 'blind delegate,' so per the task's explicit instruction (partial completion expected, don't guess), this script's build_model was left as-is. This is the one remaining piece of the original 3-script scope.

VERIFICATION: python3 -m py_compile clean on all 8 touched files (hdp_network.py, builders.py untouched/no-diff, + 6 scripts). No existing tests cover hdp_network.py/HDPColumnConfig/apply_drive_correction directly (grepped tests/*.py, zero matches) so no direct regression suite exists for this module; ran the closest upstream-dependency tests (tests/test_v0331_laminar_config.py + tests/test_tensor_pipeline_custom_cfg.py, both exercise laminar_cortex_config/tensor construct() paths) -- 14/14 passed, no regressions.

items.title: bf16 quantized-compute mode for TFNE-Izhikevich/HDP networks (not HH) + jaxfne.units.py dtype-aware defaults
items.shape:
Brainstormed 2026-07-01 across several turns; consolidating into one staged design. Scope is explicitly TFNE-Izhikevich+HDP, NOT jaxley-HH -- HH gating exponentials have a real overflow risk in low precision that Izhikevich+HDP's bounded state variables don't share, per the K_ctrl restoring-term argument confirmed below.

1. FEASIBILITY (verified, not assumed): dtype resolution is narrow -- only 2 call sites (jaxfne/core.py:368,567) do `jdtype = float64-if-x64-else-float32`. Adding a bfloat16 branch there is small and contained (rule 6 compliant: one shared resolution point).
2. BUG to fix as a precondition: `Model.with_hdp_initial_state()` (core.py:5868) hardcodes `jnp.asarray(H0, dtype=jnp.float32)` -- silently force-casts away from the model's configured dtype. Must key off the model's actual dtype instead.
3. GAP to fix as a precondition: `RuntimeConfig.dtype`'s docstring/validation is exhaustively 'float32'|'float64' -- passing any other string (e.g. 'bfloat16') today is not rejected, it silently falls through to float32 in the ternary. Must add explicit bfloat16 support + reject/warn on truly unknown values, not extend the silent fallback.
4. DESIGN (not naive full-bf16 compute): mixed precision -- compute each step's delta (dv, du, dH, dW) in float32, cast state to bf16 only at the storage/transmission boundary. Naive full-bf16 arithmetic risks *increment underflow* on a fixed-dt Euler step (dt*dv can round to exactly zero relative to v's magnitude at bf16's ~0.8% relative precision) -- a silent stall/bias, not the benign 'natural noise floor' originally hoped for. Mixed precision avoids this while keeping bf16's memory/bandwidth win.
5. jaxfne/units.py (NEW MODULE, does not exist yet -- confirmed via ls): dtype-keyed declarative defaults (epsilon primarily; NOT dt_ms/dxyz -- those are physical/discretization choices independent of storage dtype, silently changing them based on dtype selection would break run reproducibility. Emit an explicit warning instead if a config's dt/dxyz looks mismatched for its chosen dtype, never auto-adjust silently).
6. Barrier mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and matches the user's proposed 'sudden breakage near the floor' idea: jaxfne/emitters.py:1316-1318, `barrier_force = barrier_c/(H-H_min)^2 - barrier_d/(H_max-H)^2`, denominators floored by `barrier_eps` (default 1e-3). Currently DISABLED by default (barrier_c=barrier_d=0.0) and only exercised standalone in tests/test_hdp_kernel_standalone.py -- never in a full pipeline run, never validated specifically for bf16-stall mitigation. Action: enable it in the config #4 HDP-stability test (tests/test_ei_hdp_stability_rho_passive_sweep.py, already staged in plans.json item smart-test-matrix-configs-2-5) and sweep H near H_min under bf16 specifically to confirm it produces the intended 'sharp discharge' rather than a stall. Note: this only fixes stall AT the H_min/H_max boundary -- it does NOT address interior-of-range stall (H mid-range, no boundary nearby), which is what item 4's mixed-precision design covers instead.
7. Dither-noise design (scoped, not universal): add a `dither_scale(dtype)` helper to jaxfne/units.py (~half machine-epsilon at the relevant magnitude), applied ONLY at the bf16 cast boundary for quantities that are strictly positive by construction (H, tau_i, barrier denominators -- domain already excludes 0). Explicitly NOT applied to signed state that legitimately crosses zero (V_m, u, weight deltas, synaptic current) -- a hard 'never exactly zero' floor on those would inject a permanent bias into dynamics meant to pass through zero cleanly, which is a correctness bug, not a stability feature. Existing seeded jax.random.split/normal plumbing (e.g. emitters.py:397-398) is the PRNG source to reuse -- don't invent a second noise-generation path.
8. Save/load already works, confirmed no new work needed: jaxfne/_pipeline.py::checkpoint_state/restore_state (existing, schema-versioned 'checkpoint_v1') round-trips model.params/model.static via np.asarray/jnp.array, which is already dtype-transparent (numpy's ml_dtypes extension handles bfloat16 natively). Verify this holds once bfloat16 models actually exist (not yet re-verified with a real bf16 array -- confirmed only by reading the code path, not by running it).

UPDATE 2026-07-01 (Progress pass): items 5 and 7 DONE -- jaxfne/units.py built (epsilon(dtype), dither_scale(dtype), warn_dt_dtype_mismatch), 13/13 new tests pass. dither_scale is NOT yet wired into the HDP kernel (emitters.py barrier denominators/tau_i) -- that remains open follow-on work. Fixed in jaxfne/_pipeline.py (upcast-to-float32-for-storage + recorded leaf_dtypes cast-back), verified bit-for-bit with a real bf16 leaf + new regression test. Items 1-4 (RuntimeConfig bfloat16 branch, Model.with_hdp_initial_state dtype fix) were confirmed already landed in an earlier session pass. Remaining open: item 6 (barrier-mechanism bf16-stall sweep) and the mixed-precision compute design (item 4) itself are NOT implemented -- units.py only provides the constants, not the wiring.

items.title: New connectivity rule: distance/radius-limited sampling with constant target in-degree (not %-of-N^2)
items.shape:
Brainstormed 2026-07-01 during large-scale cortical column design. Confirmed real gap: compile_connection_rules/compile_connection_rules_jax's only randomized rule is 'probability' (Erdos-Renyi flat: n_target = round(probability * n_pre * n_post)) -- no distance-decay or radius-cutoff sampler exists anywhere in jaxfne/connectivity.py (confirmed via grep for distance/radius/gaussian/exp(- -- zero hits).

Design requirement (the actual point of 'localized connections'): target a roughly CONSTANT in-degree per neuron (e.g. ~1000-5000 synapses/neuron, biologically bounded, independent of total N), sampled preferentially among spatially nearby neurons (using the x/y/z positions already produced by .uniform3d()/geometry()) -- NOT a flat percentage of all n_pre*n_post pairs, which scales as O(N^2) and is memory-catastrophic at large N (see cortical-column-scaleup-ladder-100-to-1M for the exact numbers). New rule kind, e.g. 'distance_gaussian' or 'radius_cutoff', that: (1) computes pairwise distance only within a local spatial neighborhood (not a full N^2 distance matrix -- would reintroduce the same O(N^2) problem at the distance-computation step even if the resulting edge count is sparse; needs a spatial-bucketing/grid-hash pre-filter), (2) samples edges with probability falling off by distance (Gaussian or exponential), (3) caps realized in-degree per post-neuron at a configured constant, independent of N. Reuse the existing EdgeList schema (pre/post/weight/receptor_index/tau_ms) and segment_sum-based aggregation in emitters.py -- no changes needed on the compute side, only how edges are SAMPLED at construct-time.

REFINED 2026-07-01: target in-degree is a hard constant CAP of 100 connections/neuron (not the earlier illustrative 1000-5000 range) -- confirmed memory math at cap=100: N=10k -> 1M edges/20MB, N=100k -> 10M edges/200MB, N=1M -> 100M edges/2GB (EdgeList schema: pre/post/weight/receptor_index/tau_ms, 20 bytes/edge). Much more tractable than the earlier estimate -- no longer a hard GPU-memory requirement at these sizes; GPU/jax-metal now matters for wall-clock compute time (segment_sum + lax.scan over many steps), not edge-array memory.

Current confirmed state (verified this session, not assumed): NEITHER of jaxfne's two existing HDP restoring mechanisms works. (1) K_ctrl is dead code -- computed (K_ctrl_arr = jnp.asarray(K_ctrl, dtype=jdtype)) and never referenced again in the dH/dt update (jaxfne/emitters.py:1247). (2) rho_passive/H^2 fails a full 20s/5-seed sweep at EVERY one of 15 candidates across geomspace(0.005, 2.0) -- confirmed via scripts/hdp_v2_rho_sweep.py's own verdict: 'NO candidate passed all seeds'. DEFAULT_HDP as currently shipped (K_ctrl=5.0 [dead], rho_passive=0.0 [inert]) has NO active restoring force on H_i at all right now.

Required work, in order:
1. Root-cause WHY rho_passive/H^2 fails across the entire swept range, not just find a magic constant -- the F-017 ledger's own text flags 'wild H oscillation at rho<0.24, neuron silencing at rho>=0.36' as the failure MODE; understand the mechanism (likely: rho_passive/H_i^2 is a positive-feedback-prone term near H_i->0, and/or interacts badly with the alpha*I_syn income term's own timescale) before proposing a fix, not just sweep more constants blindly (that already failed once).

Summary: 100n V1 (canonical 6-layer, HDP-enabled) + 100n PFC (canonical 6-layer, generic, HDP-enabled), feedforward V1->PFC AreaConnection. V1's L4+L6 carry 30 tuned neurons (AB=10/A=10/B=10 -- assumption not yet locked, needs one-line confirmation: 10 total per class across L4+L6 combined, not per-layer). 1000ms trials, 100ms bins, fixed AAAB local-oddball structure (fx-p1=A-d1-p2=A-d2-p3=A-d3-p4=B-d4-rw). A/B = 40Hz sinusoidal drive via target_indices. Silent marker events need metadata={'drive_amplitude':0.0} (F-022 pattern). dtype float32, backend cpu. Full run = 1000 trials (1,000,000ms simulated) -- explicitly queued, NOT to be run without a separate go-ahead. NEXT STEP (not started): a 10-trial CPU smoke test, with a 10-neuron-per-column dummy-circuit fallback if even that's too slow on this machine. This work replaces docs/tutorials/05_v1_pfc_dual_column.md's old, never-implemented inter_areal_connectivity/dual_laminar_column/traveling_waves/coherence scope -- that doc's honest ASPIRATIONAL disclaimer stays in place until this new paradigm is actually built and verified working. || WEIGHT-CARRYOVER ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS (2026-07-04, code-reading only, no new sweep run yet -- part of midterm-plan step 2's 'resolve, not just mitigate' requirement): read jaxfne/emitters.py::simulate_edge_recurrent_izhikevich_hdp's actual weight-update code (lines ~1358-1361). Confirmed the exact structural gap: H_i already has a two-sided restoring term (K_ctrl*(1-H_i), revived 2026-07-01 per F-017/F-019 specifically because rho_passive alone is one-sided and can't pull H down from above H*=1) -- but the synaptic weight magnitude (wmag) has NO analogous restoring term at all, only a hard floor/ceiling clip (w_floor=1e-3, w_ceiling=50.0). This is the same class of bug K_ctrl was invented to fix for H, just never applied to w. Leading fix candidate: add a K_w_ctrl restoring term mirroring K_ctrl's form, e.g. dw_ctrl = -K_w_ctrl * (wmag - wmag_baseline) added alongside dw_exc/dw_inh in the weight ODE, pulling wmag back toward its own initial/baseline value between drive events -- structurally the same fix pattern as K_ctrl for H, applied one level down. NOT implemented or swept yet -- this is a design proposal from reading the mechanism, not a validated fix. Genuinely open questions before implementing: (1) should wmag_baseline be each edge's OWN initial weight (per-edge target) or a single global constant (simpler, but loses per-connection-class calibration)? (2) does this need its own K_w_ctrl sweep analogous to the K_ctrl sweep already done for H (scripts/hdp_v2_rho_sweep.py precedent), which is real compute work requiring its own go-ahead per the large-run doctrine? (3) should this be implemented in emitters.py (affects the shared HDP kernel, wide blast radius across every script/test that uses HDP) or scoped narrower to just this paradigm first? These are genuine multi-option decisions -- flagging for discussion rather than picking one and running a real sweep unprompted. || WEIGHT-CARRYOVER FIX IMPLEMENTED AND VALIDATED (2026-07-04, user-approved scope: implement in emitters.py shared kernel + sweep). Added K_w_ctrl parameter to jaxfne/emitters.py::simulate_edge_recurrent_izhikevich_hdp: a linear restoring force dwmag/dt += K_w_ctrl*(wmag_baseline - wmag), wmag_baseline = |edges.weight| (the network's originally-declared wiring, not the carried/chained value), mirroring K_ctrl's own form and closing the exact same structural gap (H had a two-sided restoring term, weight magnitude had none, only a hard clip). Default K_w_ctrl=0.0 (null control, fully backward compatible -- verified via existing HDP test suite, 42 tests green with no changes needed). REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VALIDATION: the first implementation pass added the parameter to emitters.py but forgot to thread it through jaxfne/_model.py's hp.get(...)-based dispatch call site (Model.simulate()'s HDP branch) -- so the very first validation sweep silently no-op'd (K_w_ctrl=0.01/0.05/0.1/0.3 all produced byte-identical runaway trajectories, which was the tell). Fixed by adding K_w_ctrl=hp.get('K_w_ctrl', 0.0) to that call site. VALIDATED on the exact V1-PFC topology: K_w_ctrl=0.001 fully stabilizes 20 chained trials with weight carryover, even at the previously-unstable K_HDP=0.01 -- weight magnitude holds at its calibrated baseline (~0.071-0.075) throughout instead of drifting toward the clip; rate stays ~12.5Hz, H converges smoothly (1.03->1.07, std shrinking to ~0.003). scripts/v1_pfc_continuous_aaab_smoke_test.py updated: carry_weights now defaults to True (was False), build_hdp_params() sets K_w_ctrl=0.001, docstrings rewritten to describe the fix (not the workaround). Real 20-trial run confirms stability end-to-end. || CONFIRMED 2026-07-05: full suite re-run after landing K_w_ctrl in both emitters.py and _model.py together -- `python -m pytest tests/ -q` -> 2679 passed, 74 skipped, 4 xfailed, 1 failed (isolated re-run confirmed: pre-existing local kaleido-not-installed gap in test_vis_smoke_all.py, unrelated to this change); ruff --select F821 clean on jaxfne/emitters.py. Committed 4c740e8 on dev, CI green, dev fast-forward-merged into main. Remaining gaps before step 2 can be marked done (see midterm-plan-2026-07-04 step 2's progress_note): no 100-trial-scale validation yet (still 20-trial), AB/A/B tagging still inline (not a reusable helper), K_w_ctrl/K_HDP still bare constants (not a named preset).

items.completion_note: First CPU smoke test implemented and run (scripts/v1_pfc_continuous_aaab_smoke_test.py), 10 trials, real receipt at outputs/v1_pfc_continuous_aaab_smoke_test/smoke_test_receipt.json. Mechanics verified end-to-end: V1(100n)+PFC(100n) NeuronalTensor, feedforward AreaConnection, fixed AAAB 1000ms trial schedule, true 40Hz sinusoidal AC drive (required extending StimulusSchedule.to_array with an optional frequency_hz event key), HDP enabled with state carried trial-to-trial via Model.with_hdp_initial_state, no NaN, stable ~12.9Hz spike rate across all 10 trials. Two design questions resolved: (1) tuning-group identity is a positional post-construction tag over the plain 'E' cell type in V1's L4/L6 (renaming to e.g. 'E_AB' would flip the excitatory/inhibitory sign heuristic in neuronal_tensor.py, which checks source_neuron_type == 'E' exactly); (2) built directly via StimulusSchedule (not the general_sequential_oddball_paradigm backbone), since full manual control over target_indices/frequency_hz per event was simpler than adapting the generic paradigm converter. NEW FINDING (real bug in the smoke-test script, now fixed, not a jaxfne bug): AreaConnection.plastic.H defaults to 0.0 (outside the valid HDP H range 0.1-10.0); construct_neuronal_tensor averages this into target neurons' initial HDP state, so an unset H on a cross-area AreaConnection silently seeded PFC's L4 neurons at H0=0.0 and blew up the HDP integration to NaN immediately at step 0 -- fixed by explicitly setting plastic=PlasticParams(H=1.0) on the AreaConnection declarations, matching the convention already used in jaxfne/configs/canonical-v1-column-1000n.json. SEPARATE GAP FOUND (genuine, undocumented, not yet fixed -- flagged for its own follow-up, not fixed inline): neuronal_tensor_to_configuration never calls Configuration.layer_fractions(), so declared per-layer Layer.n_neurons is silently ignored in favor of jaxfne's hardcoded default layer-thickness split (core._SUITE2_LAYER_FRACTIONS: L1=10%/L2=15%/L3=20%/L4=10%/L5=30%/L6=15%). This forced the tuning-group split to 25 combined V1 L4+L6 neurons (AB=9/A=8/B=8) instead of the originally-specified 30 (10/10/10). STILL OPEN: the hdp_params used (alpha=beta=gamma=delta=C_spike=0.0) is RuntimeConfig's documented 'null control' -- H_final/w_final were bit-identical across all 10 trials, i.e. the adaptation *pipeline* is verified but no actual adaptation *signal* is visible yet. Wiring a genuinely-driving HDP parameter set is deliberately deferred to avoid blind-tuning a subsystem with documented open stability issues (see hdp-stability-formula-design-and-validation). Next steps: (a) fix neuronal_tensor_to_configuration's layer-size fidelity gap as its own reviewed change; (b) find/validate a driving (non-null) HDP parameter set for this 2-area topology; (c) scale from the 10-trial smoke test toward the full 1000-trial run only after (a)/(b). || DEBUGGING PASS (2026-07-04): moved from null-control HDP to the genuinely-driving DEFAULT_HDP_DESYNC-family preset (fast tau_0_ms=5, alpha=0.05 income, gamma=0.5 rate-drain, cube-law size scaling, K_HDP dialed to 0.003). Real 10-trial run now shows CONVERGING long-term homeostatic adaptation: H_final_mean 1.048->1.063 with H_final_std SHRINKING 0.0083->0.0031, rate steady ~12.9Hz, no NaN. Key finding: the trial-to-trial instability seen while debugging is entirely WEIGHT-CARRYOVER-driven -- carrying synaptic w across trials is an unbounded positive-feedback runaway (H stabilizes rates, nothing pulls w back to baseline), reproducing F-017/F-019 at the chained level. Carrying only the homeostatic H state forward is stable even at aggressive K_HDP=0.01 over 20 trials. Script now defaults to H-only carryover (carry_weights=False), with carry_weights=True exposed only to reproduce the instability. Adaptation *signal* is now demonstrated, not just the pipeline. Remaining: a weight-homeostat would be needed for stable weight-carryover; full 1000-trial run still unauthorized.
